name: contact-center-platform

ground_truth.threatName: PII Data Exposure in Analytics and Logging

mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: PII data from customer interactions flows through various processing and analytics components without proper sanitization or encryption. This includes call recordings, chat transcripts, and customer profile data.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker with access to analytics dashboards or log files could extract sensitive customer information. Additionally, internal users with access to these systems could misuse or exfiltrate PII data.

recommendations.description: Implement PII data handling controls across the platform
recommendations.implementationDetails:
1. Use AWS Macie to detect and protect PII in S3
2. Implement data tokenization for PII fields before analytics processing
3. Configure CloudWatch logs to mask sensitive data
4. Use KMS encryption for data at rest and in transit
5. Implement field-level encryption for sensitive data in DynamoDB and RDS

recommendations.description: Enhance access controls and monitoring for PII data
recommendations.implementationDetails:
1. Implement strict IAM policies using resource tags for PII data
2. Enable CloudTrail logging for all PII access
3. Set up GuardDuty for anomaly detection
4. Configure AWS Config rules to monitor PII-related compliance

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS Macie for automated PII detection in S3 buckets. Implement AWS KMS encryption for all services handling PII. Configure VPC Flow Logs and CloudTrail for comprehensive audit trails.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Multiple public endpoints lack proper request rate limiting and could be overwhelmed by excessive traffic. The CDK code shows no usage of WAF or other DoS prevention mechanisms.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker could launch a DDoS attack against the API Gateway endpoints or Connect instance, disrupting service for legitimate users. Resource exhaustion could occur through repeated Lambda invocations or database connections.

recommendations.implementationDetails:
1. Enable AWS Shield Standard/Advanced
2. Configure WAF rules with rate limiting
3. Implement API Gateway throttling
4. Set up CloudFront with proper security configurations
5. Configure Auto Scaling for ECS/EKS workloads

1. Set up CloudWatch alarms for abnormal traffic patterns
2. Configure AWS Shield Advanced for DDoS response team access
3. Implement automated response using Lambda for threat mitigation
4. Use AWS Systems Manager for automated remediation

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Leverage AWS Shield Advanced for comprehensive DDoS protection. Use WAF ACLs to implement rate limiting and protect against application layer attacks.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: The CDK code shows broad IAM permissions and lacks fine-grained access controls for Connect integration with other AWS services. Service-linked roles are not consistently used.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker who compromises a Connect instance or gains access to an administrative account could potentially access or modify unauthorized AWS resources due to overly permissive IAM policies.

recommendations.implementationDetails:
1. Use service-linked roles for Connect features
2. Implement resource-based policies with strict conditions
3. Use AWS Organizations SCPs to enforce guardrails
4. Regular IAM access reviews and cleanup

1. Enable AWS IAM Access Analyzer
2. Implement AWS Config rules for IAM policy compliance
3. Use AWS CloudTrail for access monitoring
4. Regular security assessments using AWS Security Hub

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Leverage AWS Organizations SCPs to establish guardrails. Use AWS IAM Access Analyzer to identify unintended resource access.

mitreATT&CK: T1059.007 - Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Malicious users could inject JavaScript code through chat messages that gets executed in the context of other users' browsers when rendered in the chat interface.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker sends a chat message containing malicious JavaScript that steals session cookies or performs actions on behalf of other users when the message is displayed in their chat window.

recommendations.implementationDetails:
1. Implement proper input sanitization
2. Use Content Security Policy (CSP) headers
3. Encode all user-generated content
4. Validate and sanitize WebSocket messages
5. Use secure chat UI frameworks

1. Configure security headers in CloudFront
2. Implement WAF rules for XSS protection
3. Set up monitoring for XSS attempts
4. Regular security testing of chat interface

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS WAF with managed rule groups for XSS protection. Configure CloudFront security headers and implement proper CSP policies.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: The system relies on single-factor authentication in some areas and lacks proper MFA implementation through SAML 2.0 identity provider.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker who obtains user credentials could access the system without being challenged for a second authentication factor.

recommendations.implementationDetails:
1. Configure SAML 2.0 with MFA
2. Enable AWS IAM MFA
3. Implement MFA for API access
4. Regular access key rotation

1. Monitor failed authentication attempts
2. Implement session management
3. Configure IP-based restrictions
4. Regular security assessments

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS Single Sign-On for centralized access management. Implement AWS Organizations SCP to enforce MFA usage.

design_doc:
#!/usr/bin/env python3

# Import required AWS service icons
from diagrams.aws.network import Route53, CloudFront, APIGateway
from diagrams.aws.engagement import Connect
from diagrams.aws.ml import Lex, Polly, Transcribe, Comprehend
from diagrams.aws.compute import Lambda, ECS, EKS
from diagrams.aws.storage import S3
from diagrams.aws.database import RDS, Dynamodb
from diagrams.aws.analytics import Kinesis, Quicksight, ElasticsearchService
from diagrams.aws.integration import SQS, SNS, StepFunctions
from diagrams.aws.management import Cloudwatch
from diagrams.aws.security import IAM
from diagrams import Diagram, Cluster, Edge
from diagrams.onprem.client import Users

# Configure diagram attributes for clean, readable layout
graph_attr = {
    "splines": "polyline",  # Straight line segments
    "nodesep": "0.5",      # Closer node spacing
    "ranksep": "0.8",      # Rank separation
    "pad": "2.0",          # Diagram padding
    "concentrate": "false", # Don't merge edges
    "labeljust": "l",      # Left-justify labels
    "labelloc": "t",       # Top labels
    "fontsize": "20",      # Larger font size
    "fontname": "Arial",   # Clean font
    "bgcolor": "white",    # White background
    "label": """AWS Contact Center Architecture\n\n
    Legend:
    ─ ─ ─ (red) System Monitoring
    .... (orange) IAM Access Control"""  # Add legend
}

# Edge styling for clear flow representation
edge_attr = {
    "fontsize": "11",      # Readable label size
    "fontname": "Arial",   # Clean font
    "penwidth": "1.5",     # Visible lines
    "minlen": "1.5"        # Minimum edge length
}

# Node styling for consistent look
node_attr = {
    "fontsize": "11",      # Readable label size
    "fontname": "Arial",   # Clean font
    "margin": "0.4"        # Node margin
}

with Diagram(
    name="",  # Remove title since it's in the legend
    filename="contact_center_architecture",
    direction="TB",        # Top to Bottom layout
    graph_attr=graph_attr,
    edge_attr=edge_attr,
    node_attr=node_attr,
    outformat="png",
    show=False
) as diag:

    # End Users (positioned at bottom)
    users = Users("End Users\n(Contact Center Customers)")

    # Main AWS Account boundary
    with Cluster("AWS Account"):
        # Edge Network / Public Zone
        with Cluster("Public Security Zone"):
            dns = Route53("Route 53\nDNS")
            cdn = CloudFront("CloudFront\nCDN")

        # Application Layer
        with Cluster("Application Layer"):
            # Contact Center Services
            with Cluster("Contact Center Services"):
                connect = Connect("Amazon Connect")
                lex = Lex("Amazon Lex\nChatbot")
                polly = Polly("Amazon Polly\nText-to-Speech")
                transcribe = Transcribe("Amazon Transcribe\nSpeech-to-Text")

            # API and Processing
            with Cluster("Processing Services"):
                api = APIGateway("API Gateway")
                lambda_fn = Lambda("Lambda Functions")
                ecs = ECS("ECS")
                eks = EKS("EKS")

        # Data Layer
        with Cluster("Data Layer"):
            # Storage
            with Cluster("Storage Services"):
                s3 = S3("S3\nRecordings")
                dynamo = Dynamodb("DynamoDB\nNoSQL")
                rds = RDS("RDS\nRelational")
                search = ElasticsearchService("OpenSearch")

            # Real-time Processing
            with Cluster("Real-time Processing"):
                kinesis = Kinesis("Kinesis\nStreaming")
                comprehend = Comprehend("Comprehend\nSentiment")
                step_functions = StepFunctions("Step Functions")

            # Messaging
            with Cluster("Messaging"):
                sqs = SQS("SQS")
                sns = SNS("SNS")

        # Management & Security
        with Cluster("Management & Security"):
            quicksight = Quicksight("QuickSight\nAnalytics")
            cloudwatch = Cloudwatch("CloudWatch\nMonitoring")
            iam = IAM("IAM\nSecurity")

    # Define connections with clear labels
    # Initial user flow
    users >> Edge(label="1. DNS Query") >> dns
    dns >> Edge(label="2. Route to CDN") >> cdn
    cdn >> Edge(label="3. Connect") >> connect

    # Contact center interactions
    connect >> Edge(label="4a. Chat") >> lex
    connect >> Edge(label="4b. Text-to-Speech") >> polly
    connect >> Edge(label="4c. Speech-to-Text") >> transcribe

    # API and processing flow
    api >> Edge(label="5. API Request") >> lambda_fn
    lambda_fn >> Edge(label="6a. Container Tasks") >> ecs
    lambda_fn >> Edge(label="6b. Container Tasks") >> eks

    # Data storage flow
    lambda_fn >> Edge(label="7a. Store Data") >> dynamo
    lambda_fn >> Edge(label="7b. Store Data") >> rds
    lambda_fn >> Edge(label="7c. Store Recordings") >> s3

    # Real-time processing
    connect >> Edge(label="8a. Stream Events") >> kinesis
    kinesis >> Edge(label="8b. Analyze") >> comprehend
    comprehend >> Edge(label="8c. Process") >> step_functions

    # Search and analytics
    dynamo >> Edge(label="9a. Index") >> search
    rds >> Edge(label="9b. Index") >> search
    [s3, search] >> Edge(label="9c. Analyze") >> quicksight

    # Messaging flow
    step_functions >> Edge(label="10a. Queue") >> sqs
    step_functions >> Edge(label="10b. Notify") >> sns
    [sqs, sns] >> Edge(label="10c. Process") >> lambda_fn

    # Management connections (without labels, explained in legend)
    cloudwatch - Edge(color="red", style="dashed") - [
        connect, lex, polly, transcribe,
        lambda_fn, ecs, eks, kinesis
    ]

    # Security connections (without labels, explained in legend)
    iam - Edge(color="orange", style="dotted") - [
        connect, lex, polly, transcribe,
        lambda_fn, ecs, eks, api,
        s3, dynamo, rds, search
    ]
